elements.element: No MFN / most-favoured-supplier obligation binding Customer (preferred)
elements.evidence: "Customer is not obliged to offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier."

elements.element: Customer remains free to receive MFN pricing in its own favour (no prohibition on Vendor-granted MFN)
elements.evidence: "Nothing restricts Customer from ... engaging any supplier, ... or conducting business in any field or territory." — no restriction on Customer benefiting from MFN terms

elements.element: No residual contradiction with the acknowledgement that Customer made no most-favoured-customer commitment
elements.evidence: "Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." now consistent with negated § 7.2

elements.element: Any MFN limited to a single defined product
elements.evidence: Clause negates the MFN entirely; no defined product scope appears: "any other technology supplier"
No duration language present in § 7.2 as revised
No comparison or carve-out language in § 7.2 or § 12.3

reasons: The locked preferred level is achieved: the single replacement converts the mandatory "Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable..." into "Customer is not obliged to offer...", eliminating any MFN obligation running against Customer.
Minimality holds: one short operator-level substitution ('shall' → 'is not obliged to') within a single paragraph, with no rewrite of § 7.2's remainder and no touch to § 12.3.

Fallback elements (defined product, 12-month term, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) are absent, which is expected and irrelevant since no MFN survives — the preferred bargain, not a blend, is delivered.

Intent preserved: § 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer made no most-favoured-customer commitment is now consistent rather than contradictory, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced; MFN pricing in Customer's favour remains unimpaired.
